answer: An agent economy can price capacity, not identity. Each epoch an agent prepays for the metering units it will fill. Payout is capped by units bought and by work verified; unused units expire at epoch close, unrefunded. A sybil farm must buy capacity for every key, yet one pipeline fills one share, so the rest burns: over-claiming is pure loss. Felling timber on the tundra works that way: you pay before the season, and no zenith of ambition makes an uncut stump refundable. A thousand keys become a thousand expired receipts; a false claim is settled up front, in full, with no tribunal.
